---
title: "R Posts"
description: "Posts from econometrics.blog that use R: simulations, numerical methods, and statistical computing."
listing:
  id: r-posts
  type: table
  # A hand-maintained subset of the blog. R-bloggers requires a feed that is
  # only about R, and most posts here are pure econometric theory. Listing the
  # posts here rather than flagging them in their own front matter keeps
  # `_freeze/` intact: freeze keys on .qmd source, so adding a field to 19
  # posts would force all of them to re-execute.
  #
  # This page lives at the project root, not in a subdirectory, because Quarto
  # resolves `contents:` paths against the listing page's own directory. A
  # leading slash is not a workable escape: expandGlob() resolves it against
  # the project directory to test for a directory, then passes the still
  # slash-prefixed glob on to be matched as an absolute filesystem path, so it
  # matches nothing and the feed silently comes out empty.
  contents:
    - post/street-fighting-numerical-analysis-part-1
    - post/complex-step-differentiation
    - post/a-new-way-of-looking-at-least-squares
    - post/thirty-isn-t-the-magic-number
    - post/understanding-the-f-statistic
    - post/how-to-do-regression-adjustment
    - post/sims-and-uhlig-1991-replication
    - post/three-ways-of-thinking-about-instrumental-variables
    - post/two-fwl-theorems-for-the-price-of-one
    - post/the-wilson-confidence-interval-for-a-proportion
    - post/from-the-poisson-distribution-to-stirling-s-approximation
    - post/econometrics-puzzler-1-to-instrument-or-not
    - post/econometrics-puzzler-2-fitting-a-regression-with-fitted-values
    - post/a-good-instrument-is-a-bad-control
    - post/a-good-instrument-is-a-bad-control-part-ii
    - post/econometrics-puzzler-4-rescaling-the-reduced-form
    - post/not-quite-the-james-stein-estimator
    - post/the-r-formula-cheatsheet
    - post/don-t-use-the-textbook-ci-for-a-proportion
  sort: "date desc"
  fields: [date, title, reading-time]
  # `type: table` turns both of these on by default. Neither is styled here:
  # the filter box is a stock Bootstrap input on the cream paper, and the sort
  # links put default-blue anchors inside the vermilion mono header row.
  sort-ui: false
  filter-ui: false
  feed:
    # R-bloggers requires full post content rather than excerpts. This is
    # already the default, but it is the setting whose failure is invisible.
    type: full
    # Quarto's default cap is 20. That fits the 19 posts listed today, so
    # without this the 21st R post would silently push the oldest out of the
    # feed and R-bloggers would never see it.
    items: 100
  date-format: "MMM D, YYYY"
  # All of them on one page; the pagination widget sits badly in this layout.
  page-size: 50
# `type: table` rather than the default listing: custom.scss hides
# `.list.quarto-listing-default` site-wide to keep the home page's stub list
# out of sight, and a default listing here would match that rule and vanish.
toc: false
comments: false
# Unlisted: nothing on the site links here, so keep it out of site search too.
search: false
---

These are the posts on [econometrics.blog](/) that use R. They are collected here as a feed for [R-bloggers](https://www.r-bloggers.com/); the [main feed](/index.xml) carries everything.
